about: This is the account of the death of Hunahpu and Xbalanque. They have come through every trial of Xibalba alive, but they know that they are to die. They send for two seers, Xulu and Pacam, and tell them what to say when the lords ask what should be done with their bones: not to throw them into the ravine, for then the boys would come to life again; not to hang them in the trees, for then their faces would be seen again; but to grind them on a stone like maize and throw them into the river, so that they go off to all the mountains, small and great. Xibalba builds a great oven of heated stone, and the lords' messengers bring the boys to it. Huncame invites them to a game, to drink and to fly four times over the fire; the boys refuse, saying that they know their death is waiting there. They turn face to face, spread their arms, and go face down into the oven together, and there they die. Xibalba rejoices. Xulu and Pacam are summoned and answer as they were told; the bones are ground and thrown into the river, but they do not go far: they sink to the bottom of the water and become handsome boys again. On the fifth day they appear in the water like fish-men, and the next day as two ragged poor men, who dance the Puhuy, the Cux, the Yboy, the Xtzul and the Chitzic. They work wonders: they burn houses and bring them back at once, and they sacrifice each other and come back to life, while Xibalba crowds round to watch. Word of their dancing reaches the lords Huncame and Vucub Came, who send messengers to fetch them. The two pretend to be ashamed of their poor looks and refuse to go before the lords, and the messengers have to drive them along to the lord.

sentences.t: Are cut vae qui nabal qui camic Hunahpu, Xbalanque; are va qui nabal qui camic xchi ca biyh chic.
sentences.l: This then here their-remembrance(?) their-death Hunahpu, Xbalanque; this (va) their-remembrance(?) their-death we-shall-tell now.
sentences.i: And this is the remembrance (?) of the death of Hunahpu and Xbalanque; now we shall tell the remembrance of their death.
sentences.n: A heading of two lines, the second repeating the first: a couplet, as the openings of earlier accounts. qui camic 'their death': qui- 'their' + camic 'dying, death' (cam 'die' + -ic). nabal is not otherwise known. 'Remembrance, memory' follows Brasseur ('voici ce que la mémoire (a conservé) de la mort'), and the word may be na 'feel, know' + -bal, the ending of means, 'that by which it is known' (inferred; toggle nab'al, nothing restored). xchi ca biyh 'we shall tell': xchi- future + ca- 'we' + biyh 'say, tell', the frame of the pilot's xchicaꜯibah 'we shall write'. chic 'now, in turn'.

sentences.t: Ta xe pixabah cut, xqui bano ronohel caxcol rail xban chique; maui xe camic rumal v tihobal Xibalba, maui xe chacatahic rumal ronohel honel chicop ꜭo chi Xibalba.
sentences.l: When they-were-instructed(?) then, they-did all the-suffering, the-hardship done to-them; not they-died by its-trial of-Xibalba, not they-were-brought-low by all the-honel(?) animals there-are in Xibalba.
sentences.i: They had been forewarned (?), and they went through all the suffering and hardship that was done to them; they did not die by the trials of Xibalba, and they were not brought low by all the attacking (?) beasts that are in Xibalba.
sentences.n: xe pixabah: pixab 'counsel, instruct' + -ah. With xe 'they' and no doer it is taken as 'they had been instructed', after Brasseur ('après avoir été avertis'), that is, by the warnings of earlier parts (inferred); it could also be 'they gave their instructions', as ta xe pixabic at the end of this paragraph. xqui bano 'they did it', here 'they went through it': caxcol rail 'suffering, hardship', the pair of 014 (rail inferred). The two maui lines are a couplet: xe camic 'they died', xe chacatahic 'they were brought low'. v tihobal Xibalba 'the trial of Xibalba' (tih 'test' + -obal). honel is a doubtful word: the manuscript has a clear looped h, where Brasseur's print seems to read nonel. Its meaning is not known; 'attacking' follows Brasseur's 'toutes les attaques des brutes' (a guess; toggle jonel by the letters). ꜭo 'there are': an ink blot after chicop, perhaps a struck o, stands before it; the word is read with Brasseur's qo.

sentences.t: Cate cut ta xqui tac chi caib nicvachinel, queheri e ilol;
sentences.l: Then then (ta) they-sent-for (chi) two diviners, like they seers;
sentences.i: Then they sent for two diviners, who were like seers;
sentences.n: xqui tac 'they sent for': x- + qui- 'they' + tac 'send'. nicvachinel 'diviner' (uncertain, as in 002 and 009: an agent noun in -inel built on vach 'face, eye'); here the manuscript breaks the word nicvachi-nel at a line end, and the division as one word is doubtful (Brasseur's print is garbled here). queheri 'like, as if'; e ilol 'they (are) seers': il 'see' + -ol, the agent ending, as the pilot's ilol.

sentences.t: are qui bi va Xulu, Pacam, e etamanel: “Vve ꜭoh ꜩonoxic chive cumal rahaual Xibalba rumal ri ca camic, qui naoh ca qui nuc, rumal ri maui mi xoh camic, ma pu mi xoh chacatahic, mi xca zach qui tihobal, ma xa chicop choc chique.
sentences.l: this their name va Xulu, Pacam, they knowers: “If there-is(?) asking to-you by-them the-lords of-Xibalba about the our-death, their-thought they-are-arranging, about the not yet we-have-died, not also yet we-have-been-brought-low, now we-have-lost their-trials, not only animals let-(us)-become(?) to-them.
sentences.i: their names were Xulu and Pacam, and they were wise ones. “You may be asked by the lords of Xibalba about our death, which they are pondering and planning, since we have not yet died, not yet been brought low; we have brought their trials to nothing, and we have not become mere beasts for them (?).
sentences.n: Xulu, Pacam: names, kept. Brasseur's notes say that xulu is a verb and noun meaning 'divine' (whence ahxulu 'diviner'), and that Pacam may come from pac 'a ball, a kind of tomato'; neither is certain (toggle Pakam by the letters). e etamanel 'they (are) knowers': etaman 'know' + -el. Here the boys' speech begins; it runs to the end of the paragraph. Vve ꜭoh ꜩonoxic chive 'if there is asking to you', if you are asked: ꜭoh is taken as ꜭo 'there is' with the -oh of earlier parts (inferred, after Brasseur 'si par hasard on vous pose la question'); ꜩonoxic 'being asked' (ꜩonoh 'ask' + passive -x + -ic). rahaual Xibalba 'the lords of Xibalba'. qui naoh ca qui nuc 'their thought (which) they are arranging': ca- ongoing + qui- 'they' + nuc 'put in order'; the manuscript runs caquinuc together. mi xoh camic 'we have (not) yet died': mi marks a thing just done or not yet done, xoh 'we' (x- + oh); in the first mixoh the h is blotted and read with Brasseur's mi-x-oh. mi xca zach qui tihobal 'we have lost their trials', brought them to nothing. ma xa chicop choc chique is doubtful: choc (ch- + oc, written ch-oc across a line end) is taken as 'become', 'that we should not become mere animals to them' (a guess); Brasseur reads it 'because the brutes did not enter (the plot) with them'.

sentences.t: Are cu retal va chi ca ꜭux: chohim abah camizabal que cumal.
sentences.l: This then its-sign va in our-heart: heated stone, the-killing-instrument of-them(?) by-them.
sentences.i: And this is the sign in our hearts: the heated stone is to be their means of killing us (?).
sentences.n: retal 'its sign' (r- + etal). chi ca ꜭux 'in our heart': ca- 'our' + ꜭux 'heart'; the letter of ꜭux is q-shaped in the hand and read as the cuatrillo with Brasseur's qux. chohim abah 'heated stone', as 018 (inferred; Brasseur's note: 'bûcher, mot à mot rocher embrasé'). Here it is the great oven of the next paragraph. camizabal 'killing instrument' (cam 'die' + -iz 'make' + -abal). que cumal: que is 'of them' by the letters (que, the plural absolutive), which is odd in the boys' mouth; Brasseur takes it as 'to give us death', and the English follows him (?).

sentences.t: Mi xe cucha quib ronohel Xibalba; macu quiꜩih ta coh camic.
sentences.l: Now they-have-gathered(?) themselves all Xibalba; but-not truly (ta) we-shall-die.
sentences.i: All Xibalba has gathered together (?); but in truth we shall not die.
sentences.n: xe cucha quib 'they have gathered themselves' (?): cucha is not otherwise known; 'gather' follows Brasseur's 'tout Xibalba achève de se réunir' (inferred; toggle kucha by the letters). quib 'themselves', the reflexive with qui- 'their'. macu 'but not': ma + cu, written as one word. ta coh camic 'that we should die': coh 'we' (c- + oh), the manuscript runs tacoh together. The boys know that they will be burned and will come back.

sentences.t: Are cu i naoh va xchi ca biyh: Vue quix ul ꜩonobex xoc cumal chirech ca camic ta coh catoc, naqui xchi cu chah, ix Xulu, ix Pacam?
sentences.l: This then your-thought va we-shall-tell: If you they-come to-ask(?) entering(?) by-them about our-death when we-are-burned(?), what will then you-say(?), you Xulu, you Pacam?
sentences.i: And this is the counsel we shall tell you: if they come to ask you about our death, when we have been burned (?), what will you say, Xulu, Pacam?
sentences.n: i naoh 'your thought', the counsel for you: i- 'your (pl.)'. Vue 'if' is written so here, where the hand elsewhere has vve; it is kept as written. quix ul 'they come to you': c- + ix 'you (pl.)' + ul 'arrive here'. ꜩonobex 'to be asked' (ꜩonoh 'ask' + -obex, inferred); xoc cumal 'they enter (it)' (?), the words of Brasseur's 'de leur part'. ta coh catoc 'when we burn' (?): the manuscript clearly has c, and catoc is taken as cat 'burn' + -oc (inferred; toggle by the letters). Brasseur reads gat-oc (his g is the tresillo), 'when we have been condemned'. naqui xchi cu chah 'what will you say then': chah, with plain ch, is taken as a verb of answering, after Brasseur ('comment répondrez-vous'); the person (ix 'you') is carried by xchi, perhaps xch- + i (inferred). A vertical stroke, perhaps a later divider, stands between xchi and cuchah in the manuscript; the words are read with Brasseur's x-ch'y cu chah.

sentences.t: Vve que ꜭha chive: Ma vꜩ lo chi ca tix ta qui baquil pa zivan, vve ma ba vꜩ? Xavi xere chic chi ꜭaztah qui vach, quix ꜭha.
sentences.l: If they-say to-you: “Not good perhaps that we-throw(?) (ta) their-bones into the-ravine, or not (ba) good?” “Just so again (chic) they-shall-revive their-faces,” you-say.
sentences.i: If they say to you, ‘Would it not be good to throw their bones into the ravine? Or would that not be good?’ then you will say, ‘That way their faces would only come back to life.’
sentences.n: The first of three questions the lords will ask, each with its answer, the speech inside the boys' speech marked by que ꜭha 'they say' and quix ꜭha 'you (pl.) say'. Ma vꜩ lo 'is it not good perhaps': lo 'perhaps', as in earlier parts; Brasseur omits these three words, and the manuscript has them. chi ca tix 'that we throw' (?): tix is not otherwise known; 'throw, scatter' follows Brasseur ('jetterons-nous') and the verb's use with the river below (inferred). vve ma ba vꜩ 'or (if) it is not good'. chi ꜭaztah qui vach 'their faces will come alive': ꜭaztah 'come to life' (ꜭaz 'live' + -tah), as in earlier parts. Here the letter is g-shaped in the hand, the cuatrillo, where the same word below (chi caztah, ca qui caztah) has plain c, as in the published parts; both are printed as written, and the toggle gives k'astaj.

sentences.t: Vve ba are vꜩ xa chi ca xequeba chuvi che ta? que ꜭha chic chive.
sentences.l: “If (ba) this good only that we-hang(?)-them on-top-of trees (ta)?” they-say again to-you.
sentences.i: If they say to you again, ‘Would it be good, then, just to hang them up in the trees?’
sentences.n: xequeba 'hang them up' (?): not otherwise known; the sense follows Brasseur ('que nous les pendissions à des arbres'), and the word may be built like the -iba verbs of earlier parts (tiquiba 'plant') (inferred; toggle xekeb'a by the letters). chuvi che 'on top of the trees' (chi + v- + vi 'top'). que ꜭha chic chive 'they say again to you'.

sentences.t: Xax ma vꜩ vi; xavi xere chivil chi qui vach, quix ꜭha.
sentences.l: “Truly not good (vi); just so you-would-see (chi) their-faces,” you-say.
sentences.i: ‘No, that would not be good at all: that way you would see their faces again,’ you will say.
sentences.n: Xax 'truly, indeed', strengthening the ma 'not'. chivil 'you would see': ch- (wish or future) + iv- 'you (pl.)' + il 'see'. chi qui vach 'their faces', the chi 'at' of seeing a face; 'again' comes from xavi xere, as in Brasseur ('vous verriez de nouveau leurs visages').

sentences.t: Ta quecha chi cut chi roxmul: Xa ba re vꜩil xa chi ca tix qui baquil pa racan ha?
sentences.l: When they-say again then at its-third-time: “Only (ba) this its-goodness, only that we-throw(?) their-bones into its-leg of-water?”
sentences.i: And when they say a third time, ‘Would it be best, then, just to throw their bones into the river?’
sentences.n: quecha 'they say' (c- + e 'they' + cha 'say'). chi before cut is chic 'again' with its c lost, as in earlier parts (toggle chik). chi roxmul 'at the third time': r- 'its' + ox 'three' + mul 'times'. vꜩil 'its goodness': vꜩ 'good' + -il. tix: see above. racan ha 'the leg of the water', the river, as 007.

sentences.t: Ve cut quix vchax chic cumal: Are vꜩ bala que camic;
sentences.l: If then you-are-told again by-them: “This good indeed they-die;
sentences.i: If they ask you that again, then say, ‘That is good indeed: that way they will die;
sentences.n: quix vchax 'you are told': c- + ix 'you (pl.)' + vchax, the passive of cha 'say' (cha + -x), here written with plain ch where earlier parts have vꜭhaxic. Are vꜩ bala 'that is good indeed': vꜩ bala, the 'very well' of earlier parts. que camic 'they die', ca- ongoing + e 'they'. The seers' answer runs on through the next two units.

sentences.t: cate cu vꜩ chi hoc qui baquil chuvach abah, queheri chi queex cahim hal, huhunal cu chi queic;
sentences.l: then then good that are-ground(?) their-bones on-face-of stone, as (chi) is-ground(?) cahim(?) maize-ear(?), each-one then that is-ground(?);
sentences.i: then it would be good for their bones to be ground (?) on a stone, as maize is ground (?) to meal (?), each bone ground (?) by itself;
sentences.n: A line of three verbs not otherwise known, all read with Brasseur ('leurs os soient moulus sur la pierre comme on moud le maïs en farine, et que chacun soit moulu séparément'): hoc (in 017 'cleared', of a road), queex and queic, all taken as 'be ground' (inferred). chuvach abah 'on the face of a stone', the grinding stone. cahim hal: hal 'ear of maize', as in earlier parts (inferred); cahim has plain c in the manuscript, where Brasseur has qahim (the cuatrillo), perhaps 'ground to meal'; the letters are respelled and nothing restored. huhunal 'each one' (hun 'one' doubled + -al). The manuscript runs cuchiqueic together.

sentences.t: cate cu chi tix vbic chi racan a, chiri cah cua, chi be chuti huyub, nima huyub, quix ꜭha cut, ta chi cutunizah ri ca pixab mixca biyh chive,” xeꜭha Xhunahpu, Xbalanque, ta xe pixabic; xquetamah qui camic.
sentences.l: then then let-them-be-thrown(?) thither into its-leg of-water, there it-goes-down cua(?), let-them-go small mountains, great mountains,’ you-say then, when it-is-shown the our-counsel we-have-just told to-you,” they-said Xhunahpu, Xbalanque, when they-gave-counsel; they-knew their-death.
sentences.i: then let them be thrown into the river, there where the spring (?) comes down, so that they go off to the small mountains and the great mountains’: that is what you will say, and so you will bring out the counsel we have given you,” said Hunahpu and Xbalanque, as they gave their instructions; they knew of their death.
sentences.n: chi tix vbic 'let them be thrown away': vbic 'thither, away', as in earlier parts. racan a 'the leg of the water', the river, here with a for ha, as 010. chiri cah cua 'there it goes down, cua': cah 'go down', as in earlier parts; cua is not otherwise known in this sense, and 'spring, fountain' follows Brasseur's note ('quva, fontaine, eau cristalline') (a guess; toggle kua by the letters). chuti huyub, nima huyub 'small mountains, great mountains', a couplet. ta chi cutunizah 'when it shall be shown', brought out: cutun 'appear' + -iz 'make' + -ah; the manuscript has plain c, where Brasseur has qutun- (the cuatrillo), as in the published cutun (toggle k'utunisaj, the word being certain). mixca biyh 'we have just told' (mi + x- + ca- 'we'). Xhunahpu is written with x- here; Brasseur's note takes it as the diminutive, 'the little, the younger Hunahpu'. The English has Hunahpu (toggle Xjunajpu by the letters). ta xe pixabic 'when they gave their counsel' (?) (Brasseur 'en prenant congé d'eux'). xquetamah qui camic 'they knew their death': x- + qu- (qui- 'they' before a vowel) + etamah 'know'.

sentences.t: Are ca ban ri nima chohim abah, queheri chohibal qui xqui ban Xibalba; nimac xac xqui coho.
sentences.l: This is-made the great heated stone, like a-heating-place(?) (qui) they-made Xibalba; great leaves(?) they-put-on-it.
sentences.i: Then the great heated stone was made, like an oven (?): Xibalba made it, and they heaped great leafy branches (?) on it.
sentences.n: ca ban 'it is made': ca- + ban 'make, do', with no doer named. chohibal 'heating place, oven' (?): the chohim of chohim abah + -ibal, the ending of place (inferred); Brasseur 'semblable à un foyer demi-souterrain'. qui after it is left unrendered ('their', or the particle qui of earlier parts). nimac xac 'great leaves': xac 'leaf', as in 005 (pa xac che 'among the leaves'), here the branches piled on the fire, after Brasseur ('l'on y mettait beaucoup de branchages') (inferred). xqui coho 'they put it on' (coh 'put' + -o).

sentences.t: Catecut xul zamahel achbilai que v zamahel Huncame, Vvcub Came: “Que petoc.
sentences.l: Then came the-messengers going-along-with(?) them, his messengers of Huncame, Vucub Came: “Let-them-come.
sentences.i: Then the messengers who were to go along with them (?) came, the messengers of Huncame and Vucub Came: “Let them come.
sentences.n: zamahel 'messenger' (zamah 'errand, work' + -el). achbilai que 'going along with them' (?): achbilai as in 010 ('go along with', inferred), que 'them'; the manuscript runs achbilaique together, and the division follows Brasseur's achbilay que. Que petoc 'let them come': c- + e 'they' + pet 'come' + -oc. The lords' order begins here and runs to the end of the next unit.

sentences.t: Coh be ta cuꜭ ꜭaholab; chi be ta qui la: ca quix ca chohih, caꜭha ahau, ix ꜭaholab,” xe vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: Let-us-go (ta) with-them the-boys; let-them-go (ta) (qui la): ‘(Ca) you we-roast(?),’ says the-lord, you boys,” they-were-told.
sentences.i: Let us go with the boys; let them come along (?): ‘We are going to roast you (?),’ says the lord, boys,” they were told.
sentences.n: Coh be ta 'let us go': coh 'we' + be 'go' + ta, the wish. cuꜭ ꜭaholab 'with the boys': c- 'their' + uꜭ 'with', the boys named after it. chi be ta qui la 'let them go': qui la is not clear; la is the particle of earlier parts, perhaps the respectful 'you' (uncertain), and qui is left unrendered. ca quix ca chohih 'we are going to roast you' (?): ca- ongoing, quix 'you (pl.)', ca- 'we', chohih 'heat, roast', the verb of chohim 'heated' (inferred). Brasseur reads it so ('nous allons vous brûler'). caꜭha ahau 'the lord says': ca- + ꜭha, a saying that stands. xe vꜭhaxic 'they were told', the passive of ꜭha(u) 'speak'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good indeed,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well', the boys' answer, as in earlier parts.

sentences.t: Anim xebec, xe opon cut chu chi choh.
sentences.l: Quickly they-went, they-arrived then at-its mouth the-oven(?).
sentences.i: They went quickly, and came to the edge of the oven (?).
sentences.n: Anim 'quickly'. xebec 'they went' (x- + e + be 'go' + -c). chu chi 'at its mouth', its edge: chi + v- + chi 'mouth', as chu chi ha 'at the edge of the water' in 006. choh is not otherwise known; it is taken as the noun of chohim, 'the heated place, the oven' (inferred; Brasseur 'bûcher'). The toggle respells it by the letters.

sentences.t: Chiri cut xe rah chih vi chi eꜩanem: “Ca chopih vae ri ca quiy; cahtac mul tah chi ca xicah chi ca huhunal, ix ꜭaholab,” xeꜭhax cut rumal Huncame.
sentences.l: There then they-wanted to-force(?) (vi) at a-game: “We(?)-chopih(?) here the our-sweet(?); four-times (tah) let us-fly(?) each-of-us, you boys,” they-were-told then by Huncame.
sentences.i: There they wanted to force them (?) into a game: “Let us drink (?) our sweet drink (?) here, and let each of us fly (?) four times over it, boys,” they were told by Huncame.
sentences.n: xe rah chih 'they wanted to force (?)': rah 'want', as in earlier parts (que rah 'they want to'), and chih 'bear, endure', here 'make them bear' (inferred, after Brasseur 'on voulut les obliger'). eꜩanem 'game, play': the modern etz'anem; the tz' is supplied because the word is certain. chopih is not otherwise known; 'take, drink' follows Brasseur ('prenons donc ici nos doux breuvages') (a guess). ca quiy is a doubtful reading: the manuscript has ca qui with a raised hooked mark after it, read as y with Brasseur's ka quiy, and quiy is taken as 'sweet', the sweet drink (?). cahtac mul 'four times': cah 'four' + tac + mul 'times'. chi ca xicah 'let us fly' (?): xic 'wing' + -ah, after Brasseur's note ('xicah, voler avec des ailes') (inferred). chi ca huhunal 'each of us'. xeꜭhax 'they were told': passive of ꜭha 'say'.

sentences.t: “Maui are coh i mich vi ri. Ma pa quetaam ca camic, ix ahauab, chi vi tana?” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Not this us you-pluck(?) (vi) that. Not (pa) we-know our-death, you lords, (chi vi) tana(?)?” they-said then.
sentences.i: “You will not trick (?) us with that. Do we not know that our death is here, lords (?)?” they said.
sentences.n: coh i mich 'you pluck us' (?): coh 'us', the object, then i- 'you (pl.)', the doer, + mich 'pluck', as in 018; here taken as 'trick, make sport of us', after Brasseur ('cessez de nous plaisanter ainsi') (a guess). Ma pa 'is it not', a question. quetaam 'we know': qu- for ca- 'we' before a vowel + etaam 'know', as in earlier parts; the manuscript divides queta-am at a line end. chi vi tana is not clear: chi vi 'there, at it' (?), and tana is the unexplained word of 006 and 007 (perhaps 'wait, listen'); the manuscript has chivi at the end of a line and tana at the start of the next, and the division follows Brasseur. The English follows Brasseur's 'que la mort nous attend ici' (a guess).

sentences.t: Ta xqui culavachih qui vach, xqui rip qui cab qui cabichal, e pu hupuhuh ta xebec pa choh; chiri cut xecam vi qui cabichal.
sentences.l: Then they-met-face(?) their-faces, they-stretched-out(?) their-arms, the-two-of-them, they and face-down(?) when they-went into the-oven(?); there then they-died (vi) the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: Then they turned face to face (?) and spread out (?) their arms, the two of them, and face down (?) they went into the oven (?); and there the two of them died.
sentences.n: xqui culavachih qui vach 'they faced each other' (?): cul 'meet' + vach 'face' + -ih, 'meet face to face' (inferred), after Brasseur ('s'embrassant face contre face'). xqui rip qui cab 'they stretched out their arms' (?): rip is not otherwise known; 'spread, open' follows Brasseur ('ils croisèrent leurs bras'), and the English keeps to 'spread' (a guess). cab 'hand, arm', written with plain c (toggle q'ab'). qui cabichal 'the two of them', as in earlier parts. hupuhuh 'face down' (?): after Brasseur ('le visage en bas'); compare hupulic in 007, of going headlong (inferred; toggle by the letters). xebec pa choh 'they went into the oven'. xecam 'they died' (x- + e + cam).

sentences.t: Que quicot chi cut ronohel Xibalba, tacal qui yuyub, tacal qui xulcab: “Mi xe ca chaco quiꜩih; maui atan xqui ya quib,” xeꜭha.
sentences.l: They-rejoice again then all Xibalba, set(?) their-yuyub(?), set(?) their-xulcab(?): “Now them-we-have beaten truly; not quickly(?) they-gave themselves,” they-said.
sentences.i: Then all Xibalba rejoiced, and their cries rang out (?), their shouts (?) rang out: “Now we have truly beaten them; they were slow (?) to give themselves up,” they said.
sentences.n: chi before cut is chic (toggle chik). tacal qui yuyub, tacal qui xulcab: a couplet whose words are not understood. tacal is the 'set, landing' of earlier parts; yuyub and xulcab are not otherwise known, and 'cries and murmurs' follows Brasseur ('ils manifestaient leur joie par des cris et des murmures') (a guess). xulcab may contain xul 'flute' (?). Mi xe ca chaco 'we have beaten them': mi + x- + e 'them' + ca- 'we' + chaco 'beat it', as in 019. maui atan xqui ya quib 'not soon did they give themselves up': atan 'quickly, soon' (?), as in earlier parts; Brasseur 'ce n'est pas trop tôt qu'ils se sont rendus'.

sentences.t: Catecut qui taquic ri Xulu, Pacam, xcanah vi qui ꜩih.
sentences.l: Then their-summoning the Xulu, Pacam; was-left (vi) their-word.
sentences.i: Then Xulu and Pacam were summoned, with whom the boys had left their word.
sentences.n: qui taquic 'their being sent for': taquic 'summoning' (tac 'send for' + -ic), as in earlier parts; the t is written like an f in the hand, and read t with Brasseur's takic. xcanah vi qui ꜩih 'their word was left (with them)': x- + can 'stay, be left' + -ah (inferred); 'their' is the boys'. Brasseur 'à qui ils avaient laissé leur parole'.

sentences.t: Xavi xare xꜩonox ri xbe vi qui baquil; ta xe ꜫihin Xibalba, xhoc qui baquil, xbe tix oc chi racan a.
sentences.l: Just so it-was-asked the went (vi) their-bones; when they-divined(?) Xibalba, were-ground(?) their-bones, went thrown(?) (oc) into its-leg of-water.
sentences.i: Just as the boys had said, they were asked where the bones should go; and when Xibalba had cast the days (?), the bones were ground (?), and went to be scattered (?) in the river.
sentences.n: Xavi xare 'just so', xa are run together, as in 020. xꜩonox 'it was asked': ꜩonoh 'ask' + passive -x. ri xbe vi qui baquil 'where their bones went', the place of vi. xe ꜫihin is a doubtful reading: the letter is g-shaped in the hand, and Brasseur has gihin (his g is the tresillo); the word is taken as ꜫih 'day' + -in, 'do the days', divine by the calendar, after Brasseur ('lorsqu'ils eurent achevé leur divination') (inferred). xhoc 'were ground' (?), as hoc above. xbe tix oc 'went thrown' (?), tix as above, oc 'in'.

sentences.t: Macu xebe ta chi nah; xa huzu xecah chuxe a, e chaom ꜭaholab xe vxic;
sentences.l: But-not they-went (ta) to far; only suddenly they-went-down at-its-foot water; they handsome boys they-became;
sentences.i: But they did not go far: at once they sank to the bottom of the water, and became handsome boys;
sentences.n: Macu … ta 'but not'. chi nah 'far'. huzu 'suddenly'. xecah 'they went down': x- + e + cah 'descend' (not the xecah 'foot of the sky' of earlier parts, which has the same letters). chuxe a 'at the foot of the water', its bottom. chaom 'handsome, fine' (?): not otherwise known; after Brasseur ('de beaux jeunes gens') (inferred; toggle by the letters). xe vxic 'they became' (ux 'become' + -ic).

sentences.t: xavi xere qui vach xuxic, xecutun chi cut.
sentences.l: just so their-faces it-became; they-appeared again then.
sentences.i: their own faces came back, and they appeared again.
sentences.n: xavi xere 'just so', their faces became as before. xuxic 'it became', singular, with qui vach 'their faces'. xecutun 'they appeared': cutun 'appear, be shown', with plain c in the manuscript where Brasseur has qutun (the cuatrillo), as the published cutun (toggle k'utun). chi before cut is chic (toggle chik).

sentences.t: Chi robix cut xecutun chic, xe il chi ya rumal vinac, e caib queheri xa vinac car xe vachinic ta xil qui vach cumal Xibalba; xe ꜩucux cut chi tac ya.
sentences.l: On its-fifth-day then they-appeared again, they-were-seen in water by people; they two like only person-fish they-showed-themselves, when were-seen their-faces by-them Xibalba; they-were-sought then in various waters.
sentences.i: On the fifth day they appeared again and were seen in the water by people: the two of them showed themselves like fish-men, when Xibalba saw their faces; and they were sought through all the waters.
sentences.n: Brasseur begins his chapter 13 here. robix 'its fifth day': r- 'its' + ob 'five' + -ix, the ending of counted days (inferred; toggle rob'ix, the letters respelled). xe il 'they were seen': il 'see', the passive written without a suffix (as xil below). ya 'water, river', as in earlier parts (after Brasseur). vinac car 'person fish': car 'fish'; Brasseur's note: 'homme-poisson, the name of a kind of fish of the country', and also a kind of siren. xe vachinic 'they showed themselves', the vachin 'show a face, bear fruit' of earlier parts. xe ꜩucux 'they were sought': ꜩucuh 'seek' + passive -x. chi tac ya 'in the waters': tac, the plural marker before a noun (Brasseur's note).

sentences.t: Xchueca cut que cutun oc e caib chi meba, aꜩiyac qui vach, aꜩiiac pu quih, aꜩiiac cul qui cu; mana chi banan ta qui vach.
sentences.l: Next-day then they-appear (oc) they two as poor-men, rags their-faces, rags also their-back(?), rags cul(?) their cu(?); not (chi) made (ta) their-faces.
sentences.i: The next day the two of them appeared as poor men, their faces in rags, their backs (?) in rags, rags about their throats (?); there was nothing fair in their looks.
sentences.n: Xchueca 'the next day': chuec 'tomorrow' (chuvec in earlier parts) + -a (inferred). que cutun oc 'they appear': cutun as above, oc 'in, here'. chi meba 'as poor men': meba 'poor, orphan'. aꜩiyac 'cloth, clothes', here 'rags': the modern atz'yaq, with the tz' supplied because the word is certain. The second and third are written aꜩiiac, with ii and no y descender, and are kept as written. A '?' stands in the right margin of this line, perhaps in a later hand; it is not printed. pu quih is taken as qui ih 'their back' run together (?); Brasseur's print is unclear here (gili?). cul qui cu is not understood: cul is taken as the 'throat' of earlier parts (?), and qui cu is left unrendered; Brasseur prints qul qui qu. The manuscript has plain c and quih, which are kept. mana chi banan ta qui vach 'their faces were not made', nothing fine to see; Brasseur 'leur aspect n'avait rien d'avenant'.

sentences.t: Ta qui xe ilic rumal Xibalba, hala chi cut xqui bano: xa xahoh Puhuy, xahoh Cux, xa Yboy xqui xaho; xa Xꜩul, xa Chiꜩic xqui xah chic.
sentences.l: When (qui) they-were-seen by Xibalba, different(?) again then they-did: only dance Puhuy, dance Cux, only Yboy they-danced; only Xꜩul, only Chiꜩic they-danced again.
sentences.i: When Xibalba saw them, they did all kinds (?) of things: they danced the Puhuy, they danced the Cux, they danced the Yboy; they danced the Xtzul and the Chitzic as well.
sentences.n: xe ilic 'they were seen' (il 'see' + -ic). hala 'different, of every kind' (?): compare halahoh 'each its own way' in 002; Brasseur takes it the other way, 'ils ne faisaient que peu de chose' (a guess either way). chi before cut is chic. xahoh 'dance', the noun (the modern xajoj); xqui xaho 'they danced it' (xah 'dance' + -o), xqui xah 'they danced'. The five dances are kept as names. Brasseur's notes give: Puhuy, a long-eared owl (also short ears of maize of the hot country); Cux, a kind of weasel; Yboy, the armadillo; Xꜩul, a very venomous insect, the centipede; Chiꜩic, 'one who walks on stilts'. He adds that these are names of dances and mimes still in use among the Indians in his day. Only Yboy is the ordinary word for an animal that is certain (the modern iboy 'armadillo'); the rest are his and are not checked. Chiꜩic is a doubtful reading: the letter after chi has the shape of the ꜩ of Xꜩul on the same line, with a mark over it; Brasseur reads Chitic. The toggle respells all five by the letters.

sentences.t: Qui ia maihabal xqui ban chic: xqui poroh ha queheri quiꜩih chi catic, libah chi cut chi vinaquir chic.
sentences.l: Many(?) wonders they-did again: they-burned houses as-if truly they-burned, instantly then they-came-into-being again.
sentences.i: They worked many wonders: they set houses on fire as if they were truly burning, and at once the houses were whole again.
sentences.n: Qui ia maihabal 'many wonders' (?): qui ia is written apart, as two words, where Brasseur prints quia; it is taken as ꜭiy 'many' + -a, after his 'les nombreux prodiges' (inferred; the toggle respells the two words as written). maihabal 'wonder, marvel': maihah 'wonder at' + -abal. xqui poroh ha 'they burned houses': poroh 'burn', ha 'house'. chi catic 'they burn' (cat 'burn' + -ic), as in earlier parts (inferred). libah chi 'instantly'. chi vinaquir chic 'they came into being again', the houses made whole. Brasseur's print is garbled in libah chi cut chi vinaquir chic; the manuscript is clear.

sentences.t: Ꜩaꜩ chi Xibalba chi cayic.
sentences.l: Thick (chi) Xibalba watching(?).
sentences.i: Xibalba crowded round to watch.
sentences.n: Ꜩaꜩ chi 'thick with', the frame of 020's ꜩaꜩ chi balam. cayic 'watching' (?): cay 'look, watch' + -ic, the verb of chi ca cay 'that we may see it' in ¶7 (inferred, after Brasseur's 'à ce spectacle', 'les regardaient'; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Cate chi qui puz quib, chi cam hun chique, chi pune na chi caminaquil; nabe chi qui camizah quib, xavi xere libah chi caztah vi chi v vach.
sentences.l: Then they-sacrifice themselves; dies one of-them, stretches-out(?) first as-dead; first they-kill themselves, just so instantly he-revives (vi) at its-face.
sentences.i: Then they sacrificed each other: one of them would die and lie stretched out (?) as one dead; first they killed each other, and just as quickly he came back to life before their eyes (?).
sentences.n: chi before the verbs here marks what they did again and again, 'they would sacrifice … one would die': as in 020. qui puz quib 'they sacrifice themselves', each other: puz 'sacrifice', as in earlier parts. chi pune na chi caminaquil 'he would stretch out (?) as dead': pune is not otherwise known, and 'lie stretched out' follows Brasseur ('s'étendait mort') (a guess); caminaquil 'deadness, as one dead' (caminac 'dead' + -il). camizah 'kill' (cam 'die' + -iz + -ah). caztah 'come to life', with plain c here (see above). chi v vach 'before its face' (?), taken as 'before their eyes'; Brasseur 'à l'instant même ils se ressuscitaient'.

sentences.t: Xa qui cay Xibalba ta chi qui bano ronohel; xqui ban chic v xenacahic chic chacbal quech Xibalba cumal.
sentences.l: Only they-watch(?) Xibalba when they-do all; they-made again its-beginning(?) again the-means-of-defeat of-them Xibalba by-them.
sentences.i: Xibalba only watched them as they did it all; and so the boys made a new beginning (?) of the defeat of Xibalba.
sentences.n: qui cay 'they watch' (?), as cayic above. v xenacahic: the manuscript is clear (Brasseur's print reads u xeaaahic), but the word is not otherwise known and its meaning is uncertain; it is taken as built on xe 'root, foot', 'its beginning', after Brasseur ('le commencement de leur nouvelle victoire sur Xibalba') (a guess; toggle by the letters). chacbal quech Xibalba 'the means of beating them, Xibalba': chac 'beat' + -bal, as in 018, quech 'theirs, of them'. cumal 'by them', the boys.

sentences.t: Cate chi puch roponic chic v ꜩihel qui xahoh chi xiquin ahauab Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.l: Then (chi) also its-arrival again its-word their-dance at ear the-lords Huncame, Vucub Came.
sentences.i: Then word of their dances reached the ears of the lords Huncame and Vucub Came.
sentences.n: roponic 'its arrival': r- 'its' + opon 'arrive there' + -ic. v ꜩihel qui xahoh 'the word of their dance', the news of it (ꜩihel 'word', as in earlier parts). chi xiquin ahauab 'at the ear of the lords'. chi after Cate is left unrendered.

sentences.t: Xcha ta xqui tao: “Naqui ri e caib meba la? Quiꜩih vi chi cuz?”
sentences.l: They-said when they-heard-it: “What the they two poor-men la? Truly (vi) (chi) sweet(?)?”
sentences.i: When they heard it, they said: “Who are these two poor men? Is it truly so pleasing (?)?”
sentences.n: Xcha 'they said', singular with the lords, as often (translated as plural). xqui tao 'they heard it' (ta 'hear' + -o). la, the particle of earlier parts (uncertain). cuz 'sweet, pleasing' (?), as in 008 (quiꜩih cuz ruxlab 'truly sweet is its smell') (inferred, after Brasseur 'est-ce si agréable'); here and in Cuz xqui tao below the letter is q-shaped in the hand (quz), and it may be the cuatrillo (ꜭ). It is printed cuz with Brasseur, a doubtful letter.

sentences.t: “Quiꜩih vi pu chi hebelic qui xahouic, ronohel ca qui bano,” xꜭha cut qui ꜩihoxic xoponic cuꜭ ahauab.
sentences.l: “Truly (vi) also (chi) beautiful(?) their-dancing, all they-do,” said then their-telling who-arrived with the-lords.
sentences.i: “Truly their dancing is beautiful, and everything they do,” said the one who had brought the news of them to the lords.
sentences.n: hebelic 'beautiful' (?): hebel 'fine, handsome', as in 020, + -ic, perhaps the modern jeb'elik 'pretty' (inferred; the letters respelled). qui xahouic 'their dancing', as in earlier parts. xꜭha cut qui ꜩihoxic xoponic 'said their telling, which had arrived': qui ꜩihoxic 'their being told', taken as the news and the one who brought it, after Brasseur ('répondit celui qui en avait porté le récit') (inferred). cuꜭ ahauab 'to the lords' (c- + uꜭ 'with').

sentences.t: Cuz xqui tao. Ta xbochi cut qui zamahel tacol chique: “Petoc, chul ta qui bana ca cay, que ca maihah tah, que ca cayih ta puch, quecha ahauab, quix ꜭha chique,” xuꜭhax ri zamahel.
sentences.l: Sweet(?) they-heard-it. Then were-urged(?) then their-messengers, summoners to-them: “‘Come, let-them-come (ta) to-do-it our-watching(?); them we-marvel-at (tah), them we-watch (ta) also,’ say the-lords, you-say to-them,” were-told the messengers.
sentences.i: It pleased them (?) to hear it. Then their messengers were urged (?) to go and summon the dancers: “‘Come, let them come and do it for us to see (?), so that we may marvel at them, so that we may watch them,’ say the lords: say that to them,” the messengers were told.
sentences.n: Cuz xqui tao 'sweet they heard it', it pleased them (?); cuz is a doubtful letter (see the unit before). xbochi is not otherwise known; 'were urged, were sent' is a guess from the setting (Brasseur 'ils envoyèrent'); compare the modern b'ochi'j 'coax, persuade' (?). zamahel tacol chique 'messengers, summoners of them' (tacol, tac 'send for' + -ol). chul ta qui bana 'let them come and do it': ch- + ul 'come here', qui bana 'they do it'. ca cay 'our watching' (?), que ca maihah tah 'that we may marvel at them', que ca cayih ta puch 'that we may watch them too': a couplet, ca- 'we', que 'them', maihah 'marvel at', cayih 'watch' (?) (cay + -ih, inferred). quecha ahauab 'say the lords', quix ꜭha chique 'you (pl.) say to them': the lords' words inside the order to the messengers. xuꜭhax 'were told', singular with the messengers.

sentences.t: Xe opon cut cuꜭ ri xahol, ta xꜭhao cut qui ꜩih ahauab chique.
sentences.l: They-arrived then with-them the dancers; then was-spoken then their-word the-lords to-them.
sentences.i: They came to the dancers and gave them the lords' words.
sentences.n: cuꜭ ri xahol 'to the dancers': xahol 'dancer', xah 'dance' + -ol, the agent ending. xꜭhao 'spoke it': ꜭha 'speak' + -o; the manuscript writes xqhao, with a q-shaped cuatrillo, and Brasseur has x-chao. qui ꜩih ahauab 'the word of the lords'.

sentences.t: “Ma ba chi cah, rumal ri quiꜩih coh xobic.
sentences.l: “Not (ba) (chi) we-want, because the truly we are-afraid.
sentences.i: “We do not want to, for truly we are afraid.
sentences.n: The dancers' answer, Hunahpu and Xbalanque in disguise, runs to the end of the paragraph. Ma ba chi cah 'we do not want it': cah 'we want' (ca- 'we' before a vowel + ah 'want'), as in earlier parts; Brasseur's print reads chi ah here. xobic 'fear, be afraid': xob 'fear' + -ic; Brasseur 'nous sommes honteux'.

sentences.t: Ma xa maui coh quixbic, coh oc apanoc chi ahaual ha, rumal qui iꜩel ca vach?
sentences.l: Not only not we are-ashamed(?), we enter there at lordly house(s), because how(?) ugly our-faces?
sentences.i: Would we not be ashamed (?) to go in there, to the houses of lords, with faces as ugly as ours?
sentences.n: Ma xa maui 'would it not': a question expecting yes. quixbic 'be ashamed' (?): the quixbic of 017 (a guess there, 'fear'); here 'be ashamed' fits, and Brasseur has 'ne rougirions-nous pas'; the modern k'ix 'shame' may be the root, but the letters are respelled and nothing restored. coh oc apanoc 'we go in there' (oc 'enter', apanoc 'away, over there'). ahaual ha 'lordly house(s)': ahau 'lord' + -al. qui iꜩel ca vach 'so ugly our faces': qui 'so, how', the word of degree (as qui vꜩ), iꜩel 'bad, ugly'; the manuscript runs quiiꜩel together.

sentences.t: Ma xa qui nimac v bac ca vach chi meba?
sentences.l: Not only how great its-bone our-face, as poor-men?
sentences.i: Are not our eyes so very big, we poor men?
sentences.n: v bac ca vach 'the bone of our face', our eyes, the house rendering for vbac vvach. qui nimac 'so big'. Brasseur's note: the Indians did not usually have large eyes, so this is said in mockery of their poor looks.

sentences.t: Ma xa on ril chire xa oh xahol?
sentences.l: Not only perhaps it-sees to-it, only we dancers?
sentences.i: Is there anything to see in it, when we are only dancers?
sentences.n: on 'perhaps', as in xa on of 002. ril chire 'its seeing of it', what there is to see (r- + il 'see'). xa oh xahol 'we are only dancers': oh 'we'.

sentences.t: Naqui ta chi ca biyh chique, cach meba ꜭo cam cu raih nay pu ri ca xahoh, ca qui caztah qui vach cuꜭ?
sentences.l: What (ta) (chi) we-tell to-them, our-fellow poor-men there-are take(?) then they-want likewise also the our-dance, they-revive their-faces with-us?
sentences.i: What would we say to our fellow poor men, who are there to join in (?), who long for our dance as well, and whose faces come alive with ours?
sentences.n: cach meba 'our fellow poor men': c- (ca- 'our' before a vowel) + ach 'companion' (inferred). ꜭo cam cu raih nay pu ri: the manuscript runs gocam curaih naypu ri together; ꜭo 'there are' is read with Brasseur's qo, cam with plain c as the manuscript (Brasseur qam, the cuatrillo, 'take', that is, take part (?); toggle by the letters), and naypu is divided nay pu 'likewise also'. raih 'want, desire', as in earlier parts. ca qui caztah qui vach 'their faces come alive', they are glad; caztah with plain c, the phrase of 010 (chi ca caztah ta ca vach cuꜭ 'that our faces may come alive with them'). cuꜭ 'with us' (?): Brasseur 'se réjouir avec nous' (toggle quk'); the letters also allow 'with them', as 010 read the same phrase (kuk'). The English follows Brasseur in the whole line (inferred).

sentences.t: Ma quehe la cu xchi ca ban chique ri ahauab? Quehe cu maui ca cah vi, ix zamahel,” xeꜭha cut ri Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: Not thus (la) then we-shall-do to-them the lords? Thus then not we-want (vi), you messengers,” they-said then the Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: Is that what we should do before the lords? So we do not want to go, messengers,” said Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: Ma quehe … xchi ca ban 'shall we do thus': xchi- future + ca- 'we' + ban 'do'. la, the particle of earlier parts. ca cah 'we want': ca- ongoing + cah 'we want', as above; the manuscript has plain c, where Brasseur has ca k'ah. The English takes the line as Brasseur does ('ce n'est pas de cette façon que nous en agirions avec les rois'), the poor men's mock modesty (inferred).

sentences.t: Xelehebex na qui vach chuvi ra, chuvi cax, cacrail xebec.
sentences.l: They-were-lehebex(?) first their-faces on-top-of harm, on-top-of pain; cacrail(?) they-went.
sentences.i: With faces downcast (?) over the harm and the pain, they went unwillingly (?).
sentences.n: xelehebex and cacrail are not otherwise known. Brasseur renders the line 'à force d'être importunés et portant sur le visage les marques de leur mauvaise humeur et de leur chagrin, ils partirent, malgré eux'; the English follows him, marked (?): xelehebex is taken as a passive (-ex) said of their faces, cacrail as 'unwillingly' (guesses; toggle by the letters). chuvi ra, chuvi cax 'over the harm, over the pain': ra 'harm' and cax 'pain', the pair of earlier parts, in a couplet. The manuscript has plain c in cax and cacrail, where Brasseur prints qax cakrail.

sentences.t: Maui atan xcah benam quiamul xechihic; xa chi mach cay zamahel chi qui vach, camol que ta xebec cut ruꜭ ahau.
sentences.l: Not quickly(?) they-wanted going; many-times(?) they-were-forced(?); only (chi) mach(?) cay(?) the-messengers at their-faces, takers of-them, when they-went then with the-lord.
sentences.i: They would not go quickly; many times (?) they had to be forced (?). The messengers kept urging them (?) to their faces, and leading them, they went to the lord.
sentences.n: maui atan 'not quickly' (?), as above. xcah 'they wanted' (x- + c- + ah), not 'went down'. benam 'going' (?): be 'go' + -nam (inferred). quiamul 'many times' (?): taken as quia 'many' + mul 'times' (inferred, after Brasseur 'bien des fois'). xechihic 'they were forced' (?), chih as in ¶3 (Brasseur 'les envoyés les obligèrent'). xa chi mach cay is not understood: Brasseur prints macheay and renders 'en négociant avec eux'; the English is a guess from the setting. camol que 'takers of them' (cam 'take' + -ol). Here the part ends at a paragraph break in the manuscript; the next part opens with their arrival before the lords.
